findings.summary: TEMPORAL CLUSTER: Feb 14 'Valentine's Day Massacre' — 4 simultaneous agency cuts in 3 days. Feb 14: NHTSA (AV safety), FAA (332 employees). Feb 15: Starlink installed at GSA (bypassing procurement). Feb 17: FDA neurological device reviewers (Neuralink reviewers). All three Musk companies — Tesla (NHTSA), SpaceX (FAA), Neuralink (FDA) — had their primary regulatory oversight bodies hollowed out within 72 hours. This is simultaneous conflict clearance, not random budget-cutting.
findings.detail: The 72-hour pattern Feb 14-17 2025 represents the most compressed Musk-specific regulatory capture event documented. Timeline: Feb 14 — DOGE fires 30 NHTSA staff including 3 of 7 AV safety specialists (NHTSA is the office investigating Tesla FSD crashes), simultaneously FAA loses 332 employees; Feb 15 — Starlink satellite internet installed at GSA HQ within days of DOGE request, bypassing normal weeks/months procurement; Feb 17 — DOGE fires 20 FDA neurological device reviewers, specifically those handling BCI clinical trials (Neuralink's primary regulatory pathway). FAA cuts preceded the Feb 25 Starlink FAA contract by 11 days. FDA cuts preceded Neuralink's FDA Breakthrough Device Designation by 3 months. The cutting of the NHTSA AV office triggered no public consequence — NHTSA only opened new FSD investigation (PE25012) in October 2025.

findings.summary: PRE-WAR POSITIONING SEQUENCE: 13-month ramp (Jan 2025 - Feb 2026) before Iran strikes (Feb 28, 2026). DOGE terminates 71.1B in contracts from traditional primes (Jan-May 2025); Golden Dome created Jun 2025 (-542B program); commercial-first procurement policy instated; RTX signs 7-year framework agreements Feb 4, 2026 (24 days before first strikes); Palantir ImmigrationOS, IRS mega-database, DHS B BPA all active. Defense stocks surge on Mar 2 (first trading day after strikes): LMT +3.37%, RTX +4.7%, NOC +6%, PLTR +5.8%. Multiple Congress members on defense committees held these stocks.
findings.detail: The pre-war positioning sequence is analytically significant because the same policy decisions that appear as anti-waste/DOGE-cuts/commercial-first simultaneously eliminate traditional contractors and position tech-right companies for wartime surge. The 13 months prior to strikes: (1) .1B in traditional defense contracts terminated while SpaceX, Anduril, Palantir maintained; (2) Golden Dome created with -542B anticipated spend, favoring non-traditional vendors; (3) Michael consolidates DIU+CDAO+OSC under R&E authority — maximum single-point control; (4) RTX framework agreements signed Feb 4 (the one legacy prime that positioned correctly — RTX had 7-year commitment 24 days pre-strike). The question is not whether the war was caused by positioning — that is unfalsifiable — but whether the structure created a set of actors with financial incentives aligned with conflict, which is documentably true: every defense stock that surged March 2 was held by administration figures or their network (H64).
